description: Fields to update on the incident. All fields are optional. Include only what you want to change.

short_description.example: User cannot log in to VPN

description.example: User reports being unable to connect to VPN since this morning.

urgency.description: Urgency code. Verify the actual labels for these codes on your instance — they may not be generic High/Medium/Low.

impact.description: Impact code. Verify the actual labels for these codes on your instance — they may not be generic High/Medium/Low.

state.description: Incident state code. 1=New, 2=In Progress, 3=On Hold, 6=Resolved, 7=Closed, 8=Cancelled. Verify these values against your instance — custom/additional states are common.

assignment_group.description: Name of the group to assign the incident to (exact group name, not sys_id). Must match exactly one active group.

assigned_to.description: Username (user_name, not display name) of the person to assign the incident to.

work_notes.description: Internal note to append to the incident's work notes journal. Visible to agents only. This appends a new entry; it does not replace prior notes.
work_notes.example: Investigated and escalated to network team.

comments.description: Customer-visible note to append to the incident's comments journal. Visible to the caller and agents. This appends a new entry; it does not replace prior comments.
comments.example: We are investigating your issue and will update you shortly.

close_code.description: Resolution code. Recommended when state is set to 6 (Resolved) or 7 (Closed) — verify the exact field name and choice list your instance actually uses (this is a common source of instance-specific customization).

close_notes.description: Resolution notes explaining how the incident was resolved. Recommended when state is set to 6 (Resolved) or 7 (Closed).
close_notes.example: Restarted VPN concentrator service; confirmed user connectivity restored.
